files.origin: Live Hermes session (T17.7/T17.8): corpus inspection, schema and replay validation, plus a deliberate echo beat (identical command issued twice) and one failing tool call

beats.declare: 13 pages declared from real tool results across four tool families (read_file, terminal, skill_view, memory)
beats.fault: 1 tool_recall fault: the same sha256sum command was issued twice with identical output, so the second completion landed on an already-resident page with an unchanged contentHash
beats.error: 1 errored tool call (read_file on a non-existent path) correctly produced no page (T6 §2); hookStats records completed=25, errored=1
beats.turns: 2 turn boundaries; residentTokens 7540, headroom 112460 against the declared 120000 budget

limitations: v0 tracer is observe-only and has no eviction path (declared => resident). This drop therefore cannot exhibit page.evict, stub rendering, or second-slot paging; the eviction-shape reference remains the synthetic P-pathology vector in corpus/m1.
Faults are deduped per page and source, so repeated re-fetches of one page yield a single tool_recall row; per-turn pressure appears in call.meta rather than as repeated rows.

The recorded window starts when /ctxvm-trace start ran, not when the Hermes session began. Calls made before that point are not in the trace; skipped_untraced counts any hook that fired while tracing was off, and it is 0 here, so the window is complete for its duration.
budgetTokens=120000 is declared headroom bookkeeping (T9 convention), not the provider's measured context window.
tokenizerId is apx4-char (ceil(characters/4)), an approximation; absolute token counts are not provider usage figures.
call.meta reports providerReported=false throughout: the harness did not surface provider cache counters, so estHitTokens/estMissTokens are estimates derived from page residency.
